{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nj-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"30e9f3649abb103c384bc6ca9c3c54e84395debe85969b033d5ed886c1a9ec4c","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nj-class-d:lineage:46","source_registry_sha256":"057b72c7c679c997f56ae00ef97a6b14dbe264551f4121b9bf67b0457d9cf7c1","source_liveness_sha256":"1ca7bfbb9e3c0a6b19e5e808ecab6fe8329f3b4799e394abc260d65c1d6513e7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driver privilege and penalties confusables and continuation details","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: legal limit versus interlock threshold, first-offense fine tiers, county versus regional IDRCs, doubled-fine zones, and continuation details on abandonment, hit-and-run, fraud, vulnerable road users, driving while suspended and other violations","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: legal limit versus interlock threshold, first-offense fine tiers, county versus regional IDRCs, doubled-fine zones, and continuation details on abandonment, hit-and-run, fraud, vulnerable road users, driving while suspended and other violations
Confusable pairs among penalty rules, followed by continuation facts the C block left out for size; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A04
The adult DUI limit is a BAC of 0.08 percent, but an installed interlock blocks the engine once BAC tops just 0.05 percent. [A04]
Why it matters: group interlock; confusable legal limit versus interlock threshold.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A02
A first DUI between 0.08 and under 0.10 percent is fined $250 to $400, while a first DUI at 0.10 percent or more is fined $300 to $500. [A02]
Why it matters: group DUI fines; confusable the two first-offense tiers.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A05
First- and third-time alcohol offenders are detained at their county IDRC, whereas second-time offenders go to one of the three regional centers. [A05]
Why it matters: group IDRC; confusable county versus regional centers.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A06
Fines double for moving violations in highway construction zones, and they also double in a 65 mph zone for speeding 10 mph or more over the limit or certain other violations. [A06]
Why it matters: group doubled fines; confusable work zone versus sixty-five zone.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A04
For a breath-test refusal, the interlock runs for 9 to 15 months after restoration, compared with 12 to 15 months after a first DUI at 0.15 percent or higher. [A04]
Why it matters: group interlock; confusable refusal versus high-BAC term.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A01
Some suspensions are not mandatory and are decided case by case by the MVC Chief Administrator or the courts. [A01]
Why it matters: group driving privilege; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A06
Leaving a vehicle on or along a limited-access highway for four hours or more without permission brings a fine of $100 to $500 and possible loss of driving privileges for up to two years. [A06]
Why it matters: group other violations; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A06
Repeat vehicle abandonment raises the fine to $500 to $1,000 with a suspension of up to five years. [A06]
Why it matters: group other violations; difficulty high.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A07
A hit-and-run involving injury or death can bring a fine of $2,500 to $5,000, 180 days in jail, or both, plus a one-year license loss for a first offense and permanent loss for a later one. [A07]
Why it matters: group serious violations; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A07
Insurance application or claim fraud can be punished by fines up to $5,000, up to three years in prison, or both, and an auto insurance crime conviction also costs the license for one year. [A07]
Why it matters: group serious violations; difficulty high.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A07
Failing to pass a vulnerable road user with due caution is fined $500 with 2 penalty points if someone is injured, but $100 with no points if no one is hurt. [A07]
Why it matters: group sharing the road; confusable injury versus no injury.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A07
Lying on a license or registration application brings a $200 to $500 fine, up to six months in jail, or both, and loss of license or registration privileges for six months to two years. [A07]
Why it matters: group other violations; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A07
Driving while suspended costs $500 plus up to six more months of suspension the first time, $750 and up to five days in jail the second time, and $1,000 with a 10-day jail term the third time. [A07]
Why it matters: group driving while suspended; confusable first, second and third offense.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A08
Driving while suspended for a DUI, a refusal or as a habitual offender brings a $500 fine and one to two more years of suspension, with possible jail of 10 to 90 days. [A08]
Why it matters: group driving while suspended; difficulty high.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A08
If that same suspended driver drives on school property, through a school crossing zone, or anywhere within 1,000 feet of a school, the penalty is one to two years of suspension, a $500 fine and 60 to 90 days in jail for a first offense. [A08]
Why it matters: group driving while suspended; difficulty high.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A08
Driving after failing to install a court-ordered interlock adds a one-year suspension on top of any existing suspension. [A08]
Why it matters: group interlock; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A08
Driving while suspended for a second or later DUI or refusal conviction is a fourth-degree crime. [A08]
Why it matters: group driving while suspended; difficulty high.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0133]

FACT_ID: sec11-R18 | anchor: A09
An owner who knowingly lets someone drive whose license is suspended for DUI or refusal faces up to six months of license and registration suspension and a $1,000 fine, up to 15 days in jail, or both. [A09]
Why it matters: group other violations; difficulty high.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec11-R19 | anchor: A09
Having someone else take your license test, or taking it for someone else, brings a $200 to $500 fine, 30 to 90 days in jail, or both. [A09]
Why it matters: group other violations; difficulty medium.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec11-R20 | anchor: A09
Owing six months or more of child support or court-ordered health coverage can lead to a court-ordered suspension of both driver and professional licenses. [A09]
Why it matters: group other violations; difficulty medium.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0134]

FACT_ID: sec11-R21 | anchor: A09
A boater convicted of DUI on New Jersey waters loses boating and all driving privileges, and a first offense is fined $250 to $500. [A09]
Why it matters: group other violations; difficulty high.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0134]
